title: Feasibility of a Deep-Learning Model for Objective Visualization-Quality Assessment During Cholangioscopy-Guided Lithotripsy: A Proof-of-Concept Study

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Feasibility of a Deep-Learning Model for Objective Visualization-Quality Assessment During Cholangioscopy-Guided Lithotripsy: A Proof-of-Concept Study》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · deo270454-sec-0010-p4】A major obstacle to testing this hypothesis is the absence of objective measures of visualization quality, which has relied on subjective Likert scales; deep learning offers a route to objective image analysis [8, 9]. The primary aim of this proof‐of‐concept study was to explore the feasibility of a deep‐learning model that objectively quantifies visualization quality during EHL, and to characterize its performance honestly, including independent validation against expert labels. As a secondary, exploratory application, we used the model to compare viscous gel immersion with saline.

【Introduction · deo270454-sec-0010-p1】Single‐operator peroral cholangioscopy (POCS) has revolutionized the management of difficult bile duct stones, allowing direct visualization and precise lithotripsy [1, 2]. Electrohydraulic lithotripsy (EHL) is widely used under POCS guidance; however, maintaining a clear visual field remains a significant technical hurdle. The shockwaves generated during EHL rapidly fragment stones into fine debris and sludge that, combined with air bubbles and bile, instantly obscure the endoscopic lens — analogous to the “snowstorm effect” described in urological laser lithotripsy [3, 4].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Feasibility of a Deep-Learning Model for Objective Visualization-Quality Assessment During Cholangioscopy-Guided Lithotripsy: A Proof-of-Concept Study》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study Design and Patient Selection · deo270454-sec-0030-p1】This retrospective pilot analysis at Kagawa University reviewed records and video archives of patients who underwent POCS‐guided EHL for difficult bile duct stones between November 2021 and June 2025. In total, 15 patients were included (patient flow, Figure S3): 3 development cases, used only for model training and a convergence check, and 12 comparison cases forming the test set, with no overlap. The development cases were the first three consecutive procedures in which both viscous gel and saline were used within the same procedure, selected before the comparison cohort was assembled and solely on this mixed‐medium criterion (Table S1). The 12 comparison cases were categorized by the medium used — Viscous Gel (n = 5) or Saline (n = 7) — and each was irrigated with a single medium throughout the analyzed EHL phase. Patients with missing video were excluded. The protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board (No. 2025–238) and conducted per the Declaration of Helsinki; written or opt‐out consent was obtained, including explanation of the off‐label use of the gel in the bile duct.

【Endoscopic Procedures · deo270454-sec-0040-p1】All procedures used the same digital single‐operator cholangioscope (SpyGlass DS II; Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA, USA) and the Autolith Touch EHL system (Northgate Technologies, Elgin, IL, USA; generator M00546800; 1.9‐Fr, 375‐cm probe M00546620). In the Saline group, the duct was irrigated with normal saline; in the Viscous Gel group, a dedicated endoscopic gel (VISCOCLEAR; Otsuka Pharmaceutical Factory, Tokushima, Japan) was injected manually via the accessory channel before and during lithotripsy as needed. Owing to the retrospective design, generator settings, irrigation flow/pressure, and injected gel volume were not recorded, and injection and irrigation were not protocolized across operators (details in Supporting Information Methods).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Feasibility of a Deep-Learning Model for Objective Visualization-Quality Assessment During Cholangioscopy-Guided Lithotripsy: A Proof-of-Concept Study》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Independent Validation on Unseen Comparison Cases · deo270454-sec-0060-p1】To test generalizability without retraining, 120 frames (10 per case) from the 12 comparison cases were scored by two board‐certified POCS endoscopists blinded to group, medium, and model output; the reference was their per‐frame consensus. Frames were drawn at random while cycling through the model's predicted classes so that each class was represented, which enriched the sample for predicted‐usable frames (39% versus 13.8% of all 1950 analyzed frames). Because selection depended on model output, raw accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and κ from this sample are subject to verification bias; per‐predicted‐class positive predictive values are unbiased, so we also report binary metrics re‐weighted to the natural predicted‐class distribution (Begg–Greenes‐type correction; bootstrap 95% confidence intervals [CIs]) and results by medium (Supporting Information Methods). Metrics comprised weighted κ (5‐class), binary accuracy/sensitivity/specificity (Usable 3–4 vs. Unusable 0–2) with Wilson 95% CIs, and per‐class precision, recall, and F1 (Table 2).

【Model Performance · deo270454-sec-0100-p1】Primary (independent validation on unseen cases). The two blinded readers agreed almost perfectly (5‐class weighted κ = 0.98). Against their consensus, the model showed moderate agreement (weighted κ = 0.60). On the enriched sample, binary accuracy was 70.8% (Wilson 95% CI 62.2–78.2), sensitivity 60.7% (34/56; 47.6–72.4), and specificity 79.7% (51/64; 68.3–87.7) (Table 2 and Figure 1). Re‐weighted to the natural distribution of all 1950 analyzed frames, estimated accuracy was 73.6% (bootstrap 95% CI 63.2–83.0), sensitivity 29.8% (21.2–43.2), and specificity 93.5% (90.4–96.3), with an estimated true‐usable prevalence of 31.3% versus 13.8% predicted: under real‐world conditions the model is specific but markedly under‐sensitive, so HQVR underestimates usable time in both groups. Per medium (Table 3), agreement was moderate for both gel (n = 50; κ = 0.45; accuracy 72.0%) and saline frames (n = 70; κ = 0.69; accuracy 70.0%), with overlapping CIs; the mean signed error was −0.40 for gel and −0.19 for saline (permutation p = 0.34), i.e., no significant medium‐specific bias, and if anything the model scored gel more conservatively, which biases against the observed gel advantage. These independent metrics fall well below the hold‐out values, confirming that the hold‐out overestimated real‐world performance.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Feasibility of a Deep-Learning Model for Objective Visualization-Quality Assessment During Cholangioscopy-Guided Lithotripsy: A Proof-of-Concept Study》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【FIGURE 1 · deo270454-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 Independent validation of the deep‐learning model on 120 randomly sampled frames from the 12 previously unseen comparison cases, scored by two blinded endoscopists. (a) Five‐class confusion matrix and (b) binary (Usable, Score 3–4 vs. Unusable, Score 0–2) confusion matrix, model versus expert consensus. Overall accuracy 70.8%, sensitivity 60.7%, specificity 79.7%; five‐class weighted κ = 0.60, binary κ = 0.41. Inter‐reader agreement was near‐perfect (weighted κ = 0.98).

【FIGURE 2 · deo270454-fig-0002】FIGURE 2 Comparative assessment of visualization quality during electrohydraulic lithotripsy (EHL). (a) Saline group: a representative frame demonstrating the “snowstorm effect.” (b) Viscous gel group: a representative frame demonstrating the stabilizing effect of the gel. (c, d) Patient‐level comparison between gel and saline (n = 5 vs. 7): (c) High‐Quality View Rate and (d) mean predicted quality score. Horizontal bars, group medians; p‐values, exact two‐sided Mann–Whitney U test. High‐Quality View Rate (HQVR) did not differ significantly (p = 0.15), whereas the threshold‐independent mean predicted score did (p = 0.005).

【TABLE 3 · deo270454-tbl-0003】TABLE 3 Independent validation by immersion medium (model vs. blinded expert consensus).
